memory_update.text: AXTI should remain the primary underfollowed Layer 1B candidate for the InP substrate layer; next layer must verify InP revenue mix, non-China capacity, export-control exposure and customer qualification evidence.
LITE and COHR are better used as reference comparables for laser/InP demand and pricing power rather than as the main underfollowed discovery lane, because market attention appears high.

MTSI is a viable underfollowed component candidate around 1.6T optical links because it combines CW lasers, photodetectors and high-speed optical connectivity products, but materiality to consolidated revenue remains the key evidence gap.

FN is a capacity and qualification-cycle candidate in optical packaging and precision manufacturing; it is not a laser/substrate chokepoint, so keep it as a second-order beneficiary unless datacom optical manufacturing constraints are proven.

US-listed pure-play epitaxy equipment exposure appears limited; Aixtron is a strong tool-layer reference but is not a primary US-listed exchange candidate, so later passes should decide whether ADR/OTC or non-US listings are allowed.

node: Optical interconnect compound-semiconductor stack: lasers, InP substrates, epitaxy, silicon photonics, and transceiver assembly
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a plausible scarce-supplier universe below AI networking and transceiver headlines. The cleanest underfollowed chokepoint candidate is AXTI because it is a US-listed pure-play compound-semiconductor substrate supplier with explicit InP exposure. LITE and COHR are more obvious optical-component reference names tied to InP lasers and AI data-center optics, while MTSI is a less obvious optoelectronics and signal-chain supplier for 800G/1.6T optical connectivity. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
